subject: Redwood technical profile: sidecar egress, tenant fabric isolation, and threat-summary (BlueRock)
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: devsecops@bluerockcap.com
Date: Mon, 6 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood technical profile: sidecar egress, tenant fabric isolation, and threat-summary (BlueRock)

James —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our discussion, I’m attaching an initial network sketch describing how a typical Redwood Private deployment handles model-serving sidecars, tenant fabric isolation, and controlled outbound flows. The attachment is a lightweight PNG (redwood-sidecar-egress-v1.png) — it’s intentionally simple so we can iterate quickly.

A few things to note up front:
- Sidecar model proxies run in a hardened, minimal user-space container; they do not host persistent secrets and have a tightly scoped IAM identity.
- Egress for model artifacts and telemetry follows explicit, auditable routes (per-tenant NAT or egress gateway) with allowlists configurable by VPC/subnet.
- Tenant isolation is enforced at multiple layers: network (VPC/SG/NSG), process (cgroups / container runtime), and logical (model-serving access policies).

Action items I expect from you so we can finalize the packet:
1) Which BlueRock environment will host the Private control plane vs. the inference pool (same VPC or different accounts)?
2) Regulatory requirement: do you require dedicated HSM-backed key material (KMS/HSM) for every tenant, or is organization-level KMS acceptable?

I’m looping in Monica (Customer Success) and Karthik (Security) to provide a short threat-summary and a clearer depiction of how we contain KV cache and model state. I’ll iterate on the diagram after your feedback.

Regards,
Ethan Park
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: BlueRock Security Team <devsecops@bluerockcap.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood technical profile: sidecar egress, tenant fabric isolation, and threat-summary (BlueRock)

Ethan —

Thanks for the diagram; a few initial clarifying questions so our architects can map to our compliance baseline:
1) Sidecar egress: can you enumerate which external domains/endpoints are contacted by default (model hub pulls, telemetry, license checks)? We need a minimal allowlist for our perimeter firewall.
2) KV/cache residency: does Redwood persist KV cache to local disk, or is it in-memory only? If persisted, where is it stored and is it encrypted with tenant-scoped keys?
3) Cross-tenant inference risk: what mitigations exist if a compromised tenant attempts to probe adjacent tenant models (time-slicing, scheduled isolation, noise injection)?
4) Auditability: what logs are produced per inference request (token-level metadata, source ip, model/version id) and what retention options do you support?

We’d also appreciate a short threat-model write-up you can attach for our internal reviewers.

--
BlueRock DevSecOps

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: devsecops@bluerockcap.com, James Turner <james.turner@bluerockcap.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 May 2028 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood technical profile: sidecar egress, tenant fabric isolation, and threat-summary (BlueRock)

Hi James / BlueRock team —

Appended below is a concise technical reply from our security team; I’ve attached an updated, annotated package (redwood-fabric-isolation-v2.pdf) and an abridged threat-summary (threat-summary-abridged.txt) for your review. High-level answers: 

1) Sidecar egress endpoints (default)
- Model artifact staging: models.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS) — typically contacted only during pulls/pinned-version loads.
- Metrics/telemetry: telemetry.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS) — configurable; telemetry can be disabled or routed to an on-prem collector.
- License/heartbeat: license.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS) — optional when using offline or air-gapped deployments.
Note: All endpoints are configurable; enterprise Private installs can restrict egress to an internal mirror or block external DNS entirely.

2) KV/cache residency and encryption
- Default behavior: KV cache is memory-first (in-RAM). We avoid persistent caching on disk for session-specific KV.
- Optional persistence: for very long-running sessions customers may opt-in to encrypted local persistence; when enabled, data is written to an encrypted volume. Encryption keys can be tenant-scoped using your KMS or our customer-managed key option.

3) Cross-tenant inference risk mitigations
- Scheduling and placement: inference pods are scheduled into tenant-specific node pools where feasible; noisy-neighbor protections are applied (CPU pinning, GPU isolation).
- Process-level isolation: sidecars run under restricted service accounts and do not expose administrative APIs to user workloads.
- Rate-limiting and fingerprinting: per-tenant rate limits and anomaly detectors identify probing attempts; suspicious clients are throttled and logged.
- Canary and canary-safety: we recommend canarying new model versions in a controlled environment before wide rollout.

4) Auditability and retention
- Request logs: per-request metadata includes timestamp, authenticated principal, model id + version, route id, and a hashed request fingerprint (no raw prompt retention unless configured).
- Network logs: outbound connection records (FQDN, IP, port, TLS server cert fingerprint) are captured at the gateway/proxy layer.
- Retention: default retention is 90 days for standard plans; enterprise can configure retention up to 7 years or ship logs to your SIEM/Cloud Storage for independent retention.

Attached documents explain the attack surface and show a deployment matrix (control plane vs inference plane, cross-account options). A few operational notes:
- For air-gapped installs we provide a signed offline bundle and an installer that disables external DNS.
- Where HSM-backed keys are requested per-tenant, we typically recommend a dedicated KMS alias per tenant and rotating keys via your KMS/Cloud HSM.

Next steps:
- Ethan / Karthik: can you confirm whether BlueRock prefers an org-level or per-tenant KMS model?
- BlueRock: if you can share the target account IDs or whether control plane and inference will be co-located, we’ll produce a final annotated diagram and an expanded threat-analysis.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
